transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah, I guess the main thing is I just don’t really want to eat anymore. Like at work, on my lunch break, I’ll get something I used to actually like, and then I’m just sitting there staring at it. I end up throwing most of it away.

It’s weird because I work retail, so lunch is kind of the one break where you’re supposed to feel normal for a minute, you know? But I just… don’t. That’s what made me think maybe I should come in.
Have you been feeling down or having a low mood most days, and if so, how long has that been going on?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’s been, uh… about two months maybe. It kind of started after that window display award thing at work, when the district manager started paying all that attention to me.

I mean, the display was fine, people made a bigger deal out of it than they needed to, and after that I just… I don’t know, I’ve felt lower most days since then.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities, since you started feeling this way?

Yeah… I think so. I used to look forward to stuff like gallery nights, or playing basketball, or going to get those food-truck tacos after work. I’d help with kids’ art things sometimes too, and that used to make me feel… I don’t know, useful.

Lately I’ll go and I’m just kind of standing there, like I’m not really in it. People are talking and laughing, and I’m thinking about how long I have to stay before it looks rude. Then I usually make some excuse and leave.
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy a lot of the time, even if you’ve gotten enough sleep?

Yeah… I mean, I guess so. It’s not like I’m doing heavy lifting all day, but by the middle of a shift my body just feels… heavy. Like even straightening racks, or walking back to the stockroom, feels like it takes way more out of me than it should.

And the stockroom is always a mess anyway, like people just throw hangers wherever, and then you’re stepping over boxes trying not to knock anything down… but yeah, I get worn out pretty fast. It feels harder than it used to.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blamed yourself for things more than usual since this started?

Yeah… a lot, honestly. I keep thinking I didn’t really deserve that award, or the whole supervisor chance thing. Like people saw something that wasn’t actually there.

I know my coworkers say I didn’t trick anybody, that I worked hard on it, but it still feels like… I don’t know, like I fooled everyone somehow. And then I feel guilty, like I took attention or a chance from somebody who actually earned it.
Have you had times before this where you felt this way for a couple of weeks or more, or has this been the first time you've felt like this for a while?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, like everybody does, I guess… where work sucked or I didn’t want to deal with people. Especially around inventory time, because they keep changing how they want things counted and then everyone acts like it’s your fault when the numbers don’t match.

But… I don’t know if it was like this for weeks before. I don’t really keep track of it like that. This feels like it’s been going on a while, but as far as before-before, I’m not sure.
Have you ever had a period before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks in a row?

I don’t know… I’m having a hard time saying for sure. Like, I’ve had times where I was in a bad mood or didn’t feel like doing much, but I don’t really remember if it was more than two weeks straight.

I wasn’t really counting days, you know? Sometimes work just kind of blurs together, especially when schedules change and you’re closing one night and opening the next. So… maybe? But I can’t say for sure.
Before this current time, have you ever had a period where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks without getting better on its own?

I mean… I don’t really know. I keep trying to think back and it all kind of blends together. Like there were definitely times I was miserable or didn’t care about much, but whether it was two weeks, or if it got better on its own… I didn’t really measure it like that.

Sometimes it was just work stuff, or being tired, or I’d get through a few shifts and then feel kind of okay for a bit. So… I can’t honestly say yes. I’m not sure.
Before this current time, have you ever had a period where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks that didn’t get better on its own, even after some time passed?

I’m trying to think of something that fits that exactly, but… I don’t really know. Like, there were times I was down, sure, but whether it was more than two weeks and didn’t get better on its own… I can’t pin that down.

A lot of times I’d just keep going to work and then one day it’d feel a little less bad, or something would distract me. Like sometimes if the store got busy, you don’t really have time to think, and then you go home and it all comes back, but I don’t know if that counts. So… I’m not saying it never happened. I just don’t know.

Have you ever had a time in the past when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks that didn’t get better, even after some time passed, and you had to really push through it without things feeling better on their own?

I’m not sure… I keep trying to match it to what you’re saying, like “more than two weeks” and “didn’t get better,” but I don’t really have it sorted like that in my head.

There were times I felt pretty low and just had to get through work, like just show up and do the register and act normal with customers, and then after my shift I’d just be tired. But I don’t know if that was a whole stretch like you mean or if it just came and went.

Sometimes it’s hard to tell too, because when you’re working retail, the days kind of run together. Like if inventory was coming up or the manager was changing schedules, everything just felt bad anyway. So… I don’t know. I can’t really say I had a past time like that for sure.

Can you think of any time in your life before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, and it didn’t get better unless you really worked at it or something changed externally?

I don’t know… I’m trying to think of one clear time like that, but nothing comes up where I can say, yeah, that was definitely more than two weeks and it only changed because I did something or something big happened.

I mean, there were times I felt crappy for a while, but then work would get busy, or the schedule would change, or I’d just kind of get through the week and not think about it as much. Retail makes time weird, honestly — like you’re just looking at the next shift, the next paycheck, whether someone called out again.

So… I can’t really give you a solid yes. I’m not sure I have a time before this that fits exactly what you’re asking.

Can you think of any time in your life before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, and it only started to improve when something changed in your life or you really had to push through it?

I don’t think I can say that, not clearly. Like, I get what you’re asking — if there was a stretch before now where it stayed bad and only got better because something changed — but I can’t pull out a clean example.

I mean, life stuff changed all the time, schedules at work, different managers, people quitting and then everyone else covering shifts. Sometimes that kind of thing would make everything feel worse or keep me busy enough that I didn’t notice how I felt. But I don’t know if that means I improved because of it or if I was just distracted.

So… I’m not trying to dodge it, I just don’t really know. I can’t think of a definite time before this that fits.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, and it only got better when something changed in your life or you really had to push through it?

I mean… I’m still kind of stuck on that. Before this, I can’t really point to a time and say, yeah, that was definitely over two weeks and then it only got better because something changed.

Like, I’ve had rough patches, sure, but then I start thinking about work stuff — like how if someone quits, suddenly everybody’s schedule changes, and then you’re doing closing shifts you didn’t expect, and it messes up your whole week. So I don’t know if I was actually feeling better or just too busy dealing with that.

So… no, I don’t think I can give you a clear one. I’m not sure.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks straight, and it only started to get better when something changed in your life or you had to really push through it?

Yeah… I mean, I know you’re asking the same kind of thing, and I’m trying not to just circle around it. I don’t have a clear time like that before now.

I can remember being in bad moods or just not caring as much about stuff, but then I start mixing it up with, like, work being weird or my hours changing. Sometimes if I got put on a bunch of closing shifts, my whole sleep thing would get thrown off, and then everything felt worse anyway, but I don’t know if that counts as, like, a two-week thing or just life being annoying.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I can’t really think of a definite period before this where it was more than two weeks straight and then only got better because something changed.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks straight, and it only started to get better when something changed in your life or you had to really push through it?

I still can’t really come up with one. Like, I know what you mean — more than two weeks straight, and then something changes and it lifts — but before this, I don’t have a clear example.

I’ve had times where I was kind of low or just not into things, but then I start thinking about whether it was just because my schedule was messed up or I was dealing with stuff at work. Like if the store was short-staffed, everything felt heavier, but then once shifts changed again, I don’t know if I actually felt better or just had less going on.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I can’t say yes to that in a definite way.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks straight, and it only started to get better when something changed in your life or you had to really push through it?

Honestly, I don’t think I have a solid answer for that. Like… before this, if I felt off, I didn’t really track it by weeks or anything.

I keep trying to think back, but then I get caught on other stuff, like jobs I had or when my schedule would change, or when I was just tired from whatever was going on. It’s hard for me to separate “I was really down for more than two weeks” from “life was just kind of a mess for a bit.”

So… no, I can’t really point to a specific time before now where that happened clearly.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks straight, and it didn’t get better unless something changed in your life or you really had to push through it?

I don’t really have one I can point to, no. I mean, I’ve had stretches where I felt kind of blah or like I didn’t want to do much, but I don’t know if it was two weeks or just a bad run of shifts or me being tired.

It’s hard because time kind of blends together for me. Like I’ll remember a manager changing the schedule, or being stuck working nights, and then I’ll think maybe that’s why I felt off. But I can’t say, “yeah, that was a definite period and it only got better when something changed.” I don’t have that clear in my head.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two months straight, and it only started to get better when something changed in your life or you had to really push through it?

Two months straight? I don’t think I can really say that happened before this. I mean, I’ve had rough patches, but when you say two months, that’s… that’s a long time to know for sure.

I’m trying to think back, like around different jobs or when my hours were all over the place, because retail schedules make everything feel weird anyway. Sometimes a whole month just disappears and I only remember stuff like who was managing then or whether I was closing a lot.

But no, I don’t have a clear time before now where I was down or not interested in things for more than two months and then it got better because something changed. I can’t really point to that.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two months straight, even if you had to really push through it or something had to change for you to feel better?

Yeah, I know you’re asking it a little different, like even if I had to push through it… but I still don’t really have a clear example before now.

I can remember times where I was just dragging, especially around work schedules and stuff, like closing shifts messing up my sleep and then days off not feeling like days off. But two months straight is hard for me to say. I didn’t really keep track like that, and honestly a lot of that time kind of blends together with whatever was going on at work.

So… I don’t think I can say yes to that. Not anything I can remember clearly.

Can you think of any time before this current period when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two months straight, even if you eventually felt better without anything specific changing?

I mean… if nothing specific changed, that’s even harder for me to know. I don’t think I can point to a time like that before this where it was more than two months straight.

Like, I remember being in funks sometimes, but then I start thinking maybe it was because my sleep was off, or I was working too many weird shifts, or just regular life stuff. And then I get sidetracked trying to remember what store I was at, who was on the schedule, all that.

So… no, not that I can really say. I don’t have a clear memory of a two-month stretch like that before now.
